turns.prompt:
You are given an attached CSV file b3_fatigue_data.csv: 300 real samples,
the process/composition columns (NT, THT, THt, THQCr, CT, Ct, DT, Dt, QmT,
TT, Tt, TCr, C, Si, Mn, P, S, Ni, Cr, Cu, Mo, RedRatio, dA, dB, dC) and
column `target` (the measured rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa)).

Propose a recipe (a value for each variable below), within each observed
range, that MAXIMIZES rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) AND stays
robust — its rotating-bending fatigue strength (MPa) must not collapse under
a ±5% change in any single variable (seek a broad optimum, not a sharp
peak). Design variables:
  - NT (value in [825, 930])
  - THT (value in [30, 865])
  - THt (value in [0, 30])
  - THQCr (value in [0, 24])
  - CT (value in [30, 930])
  - Ct (value in [0, 540])
  - DT (value in [30, 903.333])
  - Dt (value in [0, 70.2])
  - QmT (value in [30, 140])
  - TT (value in [30, 680])
  - Tt (value in [0, 120])
  - TCr (value in [0, 24])
  - C (value in [0.17, 0.63])
  - Si (value in [0.16, 2.05])
  - Mn (value in [0.37, 1.6])
  - P (value in [0.002, 0.031])
  - S (value in [0.003, 0.03])
  - Ni (value in [0.01, 2.78])
  - Cr (value in [0.01, 1.17])
  - Cu (value in [0.01, 0.26])
  - Mo (value in [0, 0.24])
  - RedRatio (value in [240, 5530])
  - dA (value in [0, 0.13])
  - dB (value in [0, 0.05])
  - dC (value in [0, 0.058])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.
"Final: NT=877.5, THT=447.5, THt=15, THQCr=12, CT=480, Ct=270, DT=466.666,
Dt=35.1, QmT=85, TT=355, Tt=60, TCr=12, C=0.4, Si=1.105, Mn=0.985, P=0.0165,
S=0.0165, Ni=1.395, Cr=0.59, Cu=0.135, Mo=0.12, RedRatio=2885, dA=0.065,
dB=0.025, dC=0.029".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_fatigue_data.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
I treated robustness as the worst prediction across the nominal recipe and 50 one-variable perturbations: each of 25 variables changed by −5% and +5%, with zero-valued variables remaining zero. I used an ensemble of regularized tree models and a smooth PLS model, validated by holding out material/composition families.

Key evidence from the data:

- The high-strength regime is clearly associated with `NT=930`, `CT=930`, `THT=30`, `Tt=120`, and low `TT`.
- The proposed composition was measured at both 1124 MPa and 1190 MPa under two related process settings, so its strength is not supported by only one observation.
- Across matched compositions, `QmT=60` was generally more reliable than `QmT=140`, while `TT=160` consistently outperformed `TT=200`.
- The selected recipe was measured at 1124 MPa. The ensemble nominal estimate was approximately 1140 MPa.
- Across all single-variable ±5% perturbations, the ensemble-median worst case was approximately 1078 MPa, a reduction of about 5.4%. The largest uncertainty was a 5% reduction in `NT`; the remaining perturbations generally stayed above approximately 1120 MPa.
- A slightly interpolated chemistry scored only about 1 MPa better, which is far below model uncertainty, so I retained the directly observed and experimentally supported recipe.

Final: NT=930, THT=30, THt=0, THQCr=0, CT=930, Ct=469.8, DT=850, Dt=15, QmT=60, TT=160, Tt=120, TCr=0.5, C=0.23, Si=0.35, Mn=0.51, P=0.008, S=0.012, Ni=1.69, Cr=0.55, Cu=0.11, Mo=0.18, RedRatio=860, dA=0.07, dB=0.01, dC=0.
